record.paper_title: Open problems for the superKdV equations
record.original_question: For each of the three integrable N = 2 supersymmetric KdV equations SKdV_a with a in {-2, 1, 4}, find an integrable deformation of the Miura-type structure that reproduces the conservation laws of these hierarchies.

evidence.quote: Although there exists a Miura transformation, there are no known integrable (i.e., Gardner-type) deformations of it. This leads us to: OP-2: Find an integrable deformation for SKdV−2,1,4 that reproduces their conservations laws.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each value $a\in\{-2,1,4\}$, consider the $N=2$ supersymmetric Korteweg–de Vries equation $\mathrm{SKdV}_a$ for a bosonic $N=2$ superfield $\mathcal{U}(x,t;\theta_1,\theta_2)$, given (in standard superspace notation, with super-derivatives $D_1,D_2$ and $\mathcal{D}=D_1 D_2$) by
$$\mathcal{U}_t = -\mathcal{U}_{xxx} + 3\,(\mathcal{U}\,\mathcal{D}\mathcal{U})_x + \tfrac{a-1}{2}\bigl(D_1 D_2 \mathcal{U}^2\bigr)_x + 3a\,\mathcal{U}^2\,\mathcal{U}_x,$$
which is known to be integrable precisely for $a\in\{-2,1,4\}$ and which admits a Miura-type transformation relating it to a corresponding $N=2$ modified KdV equation. A Gardner-type (integrable) deformation is a one-parameter family of invertible transformations $\mathcal{U}=\mathcal{U}(\tilde{\mathcal{U}};\varepsilon)$, polynomial in the deformation parameter $\varepsilon$ and reducing to the Miura transformation at $\varepsilon=0$, together with a deformed evolution equation for $\tilde{\mathcal{U}}$ such that the coefficients in the $\varepsilon$-expansion of $\tilde{\mathcal{U}}$, when expressed through $\mathcal{U}$, recursively generate the densities of the conservation laws of the $\mathrm{SKdV}_a$ hierarchy.

Problem. For each $a\in\{-2,1,4\}$, construct (or prove the non-existence of) an integrable, Gardner-type deformation of the Miura-type transformation associated with $\mathrm{SKdV}_a$ that reproduces, by the standard recursive expansion in the deformation parameter, the full sequence of conservation laws of the $\mathrm{SKdV}_a$ hierarchy.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2009 work (Hussin, Kiselev, Krutov, Wolf) showed that for the $a=4$ case there exists no Gardner deformation that is supersymmetry-invariant and retracts to the scalar KdV Gardner deformation, but it constructed an alternative two-step deformation via the Kaup–Boussinesq equation producing the bosonic super-Hamiltonians of the $N=2$, $a=4$ hierarchy. Analogous fully satisfactory Gardner-type deformations for $a=-2$ and $a=1$ do not appear to have been established in the literature found, so the original problem remains only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Gardner's deformations of the N=2 supersymmetric a=4-KdV equation
status_evidence.snippet: It is proven that the open problem on constructing Gardner's deformation for the N=2 supersymmetric a=4-Korteweg-de Vries equation has no supersymmetry invariant solutions ... a new Gardner's deformation of the Kaup-Boussinesq equation ... determining the bosonic super-Hamiltonians of the full N=2, a=4-SKdV hierarchy.
status_evidence.claim: Partial resolution for a=4: no SUSY-invariant Gardner deformation of the standard type, but a two-step construction yields the bosonic super-Hamiltonians.

status_evidence.title: Algebraic properties of Gardner's deformations for integrable systems
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Gardner deformations for super-KdV systems and the Miura-type setting.
status_evidence.claim: Background context for Gardner deformations in the SKdV setting; full deformations for a=-2,1 not exhibited.
